review_basis: Blind script review by assistant before model identity reveal; not audio listening, audience research or statistically reliable benchmark. Two frozen minimal source packets. All four complete outputs failed requested 420-480 spoken-word length. Factual evaluation means source-packet adherence, not independent verification of underlying reporting.

scores.notes: Best Microsoft scene, but short. Rufus's press-release line is memorable and Alex follows him. Jamie repeatedly qualifies rather than sparring. Unsupported assertion that the code has not been independently verified; speculation about motives and premature preference for revisions.

Readable briefing, weak entertainment. Alex repeatedly paraphrases Jamie; Rufus offers analysis without a distinct comic voice. Adds oversight at key decision points, binding status and a future transparency report not established by the packet. Far short of length.

Best Gates scene. Rufus's announcement joke prompts an actual follow-up and Jamie pushes back. Overly cynical recurring public-relations framing; unsupported global-health history and claim that no independent evidence exists. Short.

Invents training/infrastructure allocation and advises applying for pilots without evidence that pilots exist. Rufus repeats a foundation-self-interest insinuation. Clear pledge versus spending distinction, but narrow chemistry and weak payoff. Far short of length.

decision_before_reveal: Prefer 1A and 2A; neither meets production aspiration. No evidence here for changing production writer.
